Heart-rate zones and reference values for MFO and Fatmax

Source: R/MFO_zones.R
MFO_zones.Rd

Expresses Fatmax and the Fatmax zone as heart rate (bpm and % of HRmax), compares the zone with the recommendation for obesity of Chavez-Guevara et al. (2023) when asked, and places MFO and Fatmax among the published percentiles of [reference_MFO] (SPEC 15).

Usage

MFO_zones(
  x,
  HRmax = NULL,
  predicted_HRmax = FALSE,
  age = NULL,
  HRmax_formula = c("tanaka", "fox"),
  population = c("general", "obesity"),
  body_fat = NULL,
  sex = NULL,
  age_group = NULL,
  weight_status = NULL
)

Arguments

x

the result of [MFO()] or the data frame returned by [MFOs()].

HRmax

maximum heart rate in bpm (optional): one value, or one per row of `x`. It takes precedence over the `HRmax` and `HR_peak` of `x`.

predicted_HRmax

logical; if `TRUE`, the predicted HRmax for `age` is used when no HRmax was given or measured (default `FALSE`).

age

age in years, needed with `predicted_HRmax = TRUE`; one value or one per row of `x`, as `body_fat`, `sex`, `age_group` and `weight_status`.

HRmax_formula

`"tanaka"` (default) or `"fox"`.

population

`"general"` (default) or `"obesity"`, which adds the range of Chavez-Guevara et al. (2023).

body_fat

body fat in % (needed with `population = "obesity"`).

sex

`"male"` or `"female"` (optional) to choose the reference group.

age_group

`"young"` or `"middle-aged"` (optional), the age groups of the reference.

weight_status

`"normal"`, `"overweight"` or `"obese"` (optional); cannot be combined with `sex` or `age_group`.

Value

A data frame of class `MFO_zones`, one row per result, with `ID` (results of [MFOs()]), `HRmax`, `HRmax_source` (`"given"`, `"measured"`, `"predicted (Tanaka)"`, `"predicted (Fox)"` or `NA`), `FAT_MAX` and the zone (`zone_lower`, `zone_upper`; % VO2max), `FAT_MAX_HR`, `zone_lower_HR`, `zone_upper_HR` (bpm), `FAT_MAX_porcHRmax`, `zone_lower_porcHRmax`, `zone_upper_porcHRmax`, `obesity_range_lower`, `obesity_range_upper` and `obesity_zone` (`NA` unless `population = "obesity"`), `MFO`, `MFO_percentile`, `MFO_percentile_label`, `Fatmax_percentile`, `Fatmax_percentile_label`, `reference`, `reference_n` and `reference_differences`.

HRmax

The HRmax used for the percentages is, in this order: `HRmax` given here or in [MFO()]/[MFOs()]; the peak HR measured in the graded test (`HR_peak`, the highest mean HR over the same window as VO2max); and, only when `predicted_HRmax = TRUE`, the predicted HRmax for `age`: `"tanaka"` 208 - 0.7 x age (default; Tanaka, Monahan and Seals 2001, doi:10.1016/s0735-1097(00)01054-8 ) or `"fox"` 220 - age, the equation in common use described by Tanaka, Monahan and Seals (2001). The column `HRmax_source` says which one was used.

Obesity

With `population = "obesity"`, the zone in % HRmax is compared with the range of Chavez-Guevara et al. (2023, doi:10.1007/s40279-023-01897-y ): 61-66 % HRpeak with more than 35 % body fat and 57-64 % HRpeak with less than 35 %; `body_fat` chooses the range. The source does not cover exactly 35.0 %: there is no range (`NA`), with a message. `obesity_zone` is `"inside"` (the whole zone falls in the range), `"partly overlaps"` or `"outside"`. The range refers to the measured HRpeak: with a predicted HRmax it is still shown, with a warning.

Reference values

MFO (g/min) and Fatmax (% VO2max) are placed among the empirical percentiles P20, P40, P60 and P80 of Table 1 of Amaro-Gahete, Sanchez-Delgado and Ruiz (2018, doi:10.3389/fphys.2018.01460 ), 167 sedentary adults, by linear interpolation. Below P20 or above P80 the label is `"< P20"` or `"> P80"` and the percentile `NA`: there is no extrapolation. A percentile is never returned without its group (`reference`, `reference_n`).

The group is chosen with `sex`, `age_group` and `weight_status`, only in the combinations Table 1 prints: sex, age group, sex and age group, or weight status. The source does not publish the age or BMI cut-offs of its groups (young adults 22.1 +/- 2.2 years, middle-aged adults 52.1 +/- 4.6 years), so the group is never deduced from a numeric age or BMI.

The reference was measured walking on a treadmill. Results with `mode = "walking"` or `"running"` get a percentile; with `"cycling"` the percentile is `NA`, because the mode of exercise changes MFO and Fatmax (Amaro-Gahete et al. 2018). `reference_differences` lists how the test differs from the reference: mode, equation (Frayn without protein in the reference), protocol (3-min steps averaged over the last 60 s), method (third-degree polynomial through the origin in the reference, unlike the unconstrained `"P3"` of [MFO()]) and fasting (5-6 h, not overnight).

References

Amaro-Gahete FJ, Sanchez-Delgado G, Ruiz JR (2018). Commentary: Contextualising maximal fat oxidation during exercise: determinants and normative values. Front Physiol 9: 1460, Table 1. doi:10.3389/fphys.2018.01460

Chavez-Guevara IA, Amaro-Gahete FJ, Ramos-Jimenez A, Brun JF (2023). Toward exercise guidelines for optimizing fat oxidation during exercise in obesity: a systematic review and meta-regression. Sports Med 53(12): 2399-2416. doi:10.1007/s40279-023-01897-y

Tanaka H, Monahan KD, Seals DR (2001). Age-predicted maximal heart rate revisited. J Am Coll Cardiol 37(1): 153-156. doi:10.1016/s0735-1097(00)01054-8

See also

[MFO()], [MFOs()], [reference_MFO]

Examples

data(list = c("MFO_df", "basal_df", "VO2max_df"), package = "MFO")
res <- suppressWarnings(MFO(step_time = 20, db_MFO = MFO_df,
                            db_basal = basal_df, db_graded = VO2max_df,
                            cv_var = "RER", author = "Frayn"))
#> Kcal uses energy_equivalents = "classic" (4 kcal/g CHO, 9 kcal/g FAT). The default will change to "source" (values of the equation's source) in MFO 0.3.0. Set energy_equivalents explicitly to silence this message (shown once per session).
#> VO2max: a 30-s window is not a multiple of step_time (20 s); using 2 record(s) = 40 s.
#> VO2max_type: age not given, so the heart-rate criterion of VO2max is not evaluated and VO2max is labelled from the plateau only. Set age to evaluate it (shown once per session).
# MFO_df is a cycling test: zones in HR, but no percentile, because the
# reference was measured walking on a treadmill
MFO_zones(res, sex = "male", age_group = "young")
#> No percentile for 1 result(s) with mode "cycling": the reference (Amaro-Gahete et al. 2018) was measured walking on a treadmill, and the mode of exercise changes MFO and Fatmax. Set MFO_protocol(mode = ) if the test was walking or running.
#> MFO zones
#>   Fatmax:      36.2% VO2max, 128 bpm, 69.5% HRmax
#>   Fatmax zone: 24.2-48.3% VO2max, 107-145 bpm, 57.9-78.4% HRmax
#>   HRmax:       185 bpm (measured)
#>   Reference:   Amaro-Gahete 2018: Sedentary young adult men (n = 41)
#>     MFO 0.32 g/min: no percentile
#>     Fatmax 36.2 % VO2max: no percentile
#>     Differences: mode: cycling (reference: treadmill walking; no percentile); method: P3 (reference: third-degree polynomial through (0;0), Croci et al. 2014); fasting: reference 5-6 h, not overnight
# Range for obesity of Chavez-Guevara et al. (2023)
MFO_zones(res, population = "obesity", body_fat = 38)
#> No percentile for 1 result(s) with mode "cycling": the reference (Amaro-Gahete et al. 2018) was measured walking on a treadmill, and the mode of exercise changes MFO and Fatmax. Set MFO_protocol(mode = ) if the test was walking or running.
#> MFO zones
#>   Fatmax:      36.2% VO2max, 128 bpm, 69.5% HRmax
#>   Fatmax zone: 24.2-48.3% VO2max, 107-145 bpm, 57.9-78.4% HRmax
#>   HRmax:       185 bpm (measured)
#>   Obesity range (Chavez-Guevara et al. 2023): 61-66% HRpeak; zone partly overlaps
#>   Reference:   Amaro-Gahete 2018: Sedentary adults (n = 167)
#>     MFO 0.32 g/min: no percentile
#>     Fatmax 36.2 % VO2max: no percentile
#>     Differences: mode: cycling (reference: treadmill walking; no percentile); method: P3 (reference: third-degree polynomial through (0;0), Croci et al. 2014); fasting: reference 5-6 h, not overnight
